metadata.description: `by-name/<name>.json` — the candidate set for one bare package name, epoch 1 (PROP-008 §2.8): every package sharing that short name in one HTTP GET, each carrying its own `group`. Root type `NameEntry`; the per-version records inside `packages[].versions[]` are the shared `version_entry` vocabulary. Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/index/e1/by_name/`.

One entry per `group` publishing a package called `name`, sorted by `group`; a length greater than one is a short-name collision (PROP-008 §2.7). The writer has no `skip_serializing_if`, so an empty candidate set is emitted as `[]`, never omitted.

Present when this bare name is a short spelling the REGISTRY OWNER offers for another package (PROP-008 §2.6): `by-name/qwen.json` carrying `alias = { group: "org.vibevm.qwen", name: "qwen-code" }` says the spelling `qwen` means that package. Authored only in the registry's own `aliases.toml` — a package cannot declare its own alias. It rides BESIDE `packages[]` rather than inside it, and that placement is the whole compatibility story: a reader that has never heard of aliases sees the candidate set it always saw (empty, for a pure alias) and says the name is not there, which is the truthful answer for a reader that cannot follow the pointer — where an alias smuggled in as a candidate would have been read as a real package of that name. `packages[]` outranks it for every reader: a name somebody publishes is never displaced by a spelling somebody offers.

One package — every indexed version of a single `(group, name)` identity (PROP-008 §2.2). Local to this schema: nothing else consumes the aggregate (`journal` carries `version_entry` directly, not the per-name rollup).
Sorted ascending by `version`. No `skip_serializing_if` on the writer, so the list is emitted even when empty.
Newest non-prerelease version, recomputed by `finalise()`; absent when every version is a prerelease or the list is empty.

The package a short spelling stands for — the fully qualified `(group, name)` identity of PROP-008 §2.2, and never a version: an alias is a spelling of a PACKAGE, so version selection stays the operator's. Local to this schema: the alias table that authors these rows is TOML, not wire, and nothing else consumes the pointer.
A name's death record — its reason for being gone and, when known, the successor to move to (PROP-044 §2, the no-silence law). Local to this schema: `NameEntry` is its only consumer.
The successor this name's consumers should move to — a redirect pointer, never an automatic rewrite.
